question: Can a portable replay of the public 306B ARAP correction reduce the known carrier distortion while query points interpolate only through original source triangles?
design: Retrospective engineering control. Published before/after summaries and the right-group defect were known before this protocol. No independent discovery or ink-efficacy test.

arms.A: Published touch-up reconstructed before ARAP, including float32 roundtrip
arms.B: Unchanged published ARAP settings, rigid alignment and LinearNDInterpolator
arms.C: Same saved ARAP UV solution as B, inverse rasterization through original triangles only

replay.on_failure: Stop before C; retain A, B, target and receipt; no tolerance or parameter revision in this experiment

provenance.arithmetic_scope: Float64 in-memory samples before TIFF serialization; report float32 rounding separately

support_perturbation.center: published fixed vertex in original carrier row/column
support_perturbation.hole_queries: Full C valid queries whose source triangle has all three vertices removed and all barycentric weights exceed 1e-6
support_perturbation.interpretation: Designed removal of support on a real public mesh, not observed manuscript damage

metrics.primary: A/B/C four-corner common cells in the fixed published right group; same target-grid positions, not exact material correspondence
metrics.secondary: Original publisher three-corner summaries in four fixed regions; full original-triangle singular values and area before/after UV on identical triangles; all flips, degeneracies, losses and per-component counts retained
metrics.B_C_difference: Decoded float32 XYZ differences in common support, in source voxels and micrometres; different triangulations are not evidence of improved truth

decision: All gates passing permits one bounded, matched public-known-text CT/ink comparison. Any failure retains the failed gate and blocks unattended adoption. Geometry success never establishes ink improvement, a new reading, a physical sheet face, global injectivity or prize qualification.
